record.paper_title: Some Open Problems on Multiple Ergodic Averages
record.original_question: Let c, c1, ..., cℓ be positive real numbers. Do the prime numbers contain infinitely many configurations of the form {m, m + [n^c], m + 2[n^c], ..., m + ℓ[n^c]} and, more generally, {m, m + [n^{c1}], ..., m + [n^{cℓ}]}?

evidence.quote: Problem 30. Let ` ∈ N and c, c1, . . . , c` be positive real numbers. Show that the prime numbers contain patterns of the form {m, m + [n^c], m + 2[n^c], . . . , m + `[n^c]} and {m, m + [n^c1], . . . , m + [n^c`]} for infinitely many n ∈ N.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\ell \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $c, c_1, \ldots, c_\ell$ be positive real numbers. For a real number $x$, let $[x]$ denote the integer part (floor) of $x$. Let $\mathbb{P}$ denote the set of prime numbers.

(a) Show that there exist infinitely many $n \in \mathbb{N}$ such that there is some $m \in \mathbb{N}$ for which all of
$$m,\ m + [n^c],\ m + 2[n^c],\ \ldots,\ m + \ell[n^c]$$
are prime, i.e., $\mathbb{P}$ contains infinitely many $(\ell+1)$-term arithmetic progressions whose common difference is of the form $[n^c]$.

(b) More generally, show that there exist infinitely many $n \in \mathbb{N}$ such that there is some $m \in \mathbb{N}$ for which all of
$$m,\ m + [n^{c_1}],\ m + [n^{c_2}],\ \ldots,\ m + [n^{c_\ell}]$$
are prime.
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution was found. The Green–Tao theorem gives arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions in the primes, and Tao–Ziegler extends this to polynomial progressions with integer-valued polynomials, but neither covers common differences of the fractional-power form $[n^c]$ for arbitrary positive real $c$. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: The primes contain arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions (Green–Tao)
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes arbitrarily long APs in the primes, but with no Hardy-field constraint on the common difference.
status_evidence.claim: Existing prime AP results do not address the floor-of-power constraint $[n^c]$.

status_evidence.title: Green–Tao theorem - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Tao and Ziegler extended Green–Tao to polynomial progressions with integer-valued polynomials.
status_evidence.claim: Extensions to polynomial progressions exist, but configurations with step $[n^c]$ for real $c>0$ are not covered.
